title: Eventual finite generation from a fixed finite affine section cover
statement: Let X be a compact separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let M be an invertible O_X-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and G a finite type quasi-coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let I be a finite index type and s_i : O_X -> M global sections. Suppose the opens U_i = X minus the support of Z(s_i) [def-pc-zero-scheme] are affine and cover X. Then there is K in N such that for every k>=K, G tensor M^k [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] has a finite family of global generating sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], equivalently an epimorphic evaluation map from a finite free sheaf. This is only the fixed-degree local-generator extension argument; no ampleness or residue-class assertion is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.5, p. 85, last proof paragraph, from the finite affine X_fi cover through generation of F(km); specialize the already common tensor degree to one. Clearing denominators is Stacks Properties Lemma 01PW.

proof.text: Put U_i = X minus the support of Z(s_i). Restrict G to these affine opens. Quasi-coherence and finite type restrict to opens: restrict the local finite free surjections. Apply lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-type-generating-sections to U_i.toScheme to choose a finite family t_ij generating G|U_i. This is a choice inside a proposition, not a definition of data from a holed existence theorem.

Use the terminal morphism X -> Spec Z. The separatedness and compactness assumptions satisfy lem-pc-section-clearing-denominators. For each local generator t_ij obtain a_ij >= 0 and a global section v_ij of G tensor M^a_ij restricting to t_ij tensor s_i^a_ij. Let K be the maximum of this finite family of exponents (K=0 if the family is empty).

For each k >= K multiply v_ij by s_i^(k-a_ij), using the associator and the tensor-power addition isomorphism, to obtain u_ij(k) in Gamma(X,G tensor M^k). Naturality of tensor restriction and the identity a_ij+(k-a_ij)=k show that u_ij(k)|U_i = t_ij tensor s_i^k. On U_i the section s_i generates M: the proved isFreeGenerator_app_one_of_le in the clearing-denominators module establishes this directly from the zero-locus convention. Its k-th tensor power is a free generator, including k=0.

Tensoring with this free generator identifies G|U_i with (G tensor M^k)|U_i and carries each t_ij to u_ij(k)|U_i. Hence the latter family generates on U_i. Take the finite union over i,j and form its evaluation map from the free sheaf. Its restriction to U_i contains the surjection from the i-th generating family, so it is locally surjective on every U_i. As these opens cover X it is locally surjective everywhere and thus epi, by lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks. This gives finite GeneratingSections for each k>=K. If X is empty the empty evaluation map is epi; if G=0 an empty family suffices. No positive lower bound on k is needed.

    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [X.IsSeparated]
    (M G : X.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] [G.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsFiniteType]
    {I : Type u} [Finite I] (s : I → (𝟙_ X.Modules ⟶ M))

    ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, K ≤ k →
      ∃ σ : (tensorObj G (M.tensorPow k)).GeneratingSections, σ.IsFiniteType
